/ai-landing-page-builder/landing-page-se.note: [truth | HUB_RULES 8] feature_5: Escalated from reviewer-batch-m1's note because it is untrue, not merely imprecise. Organic search clicks carry no UTM tags, so filtering a form's UTM field separates tagged paid leads from every untagged lead: direct, referral, email and organic together. The cited source (support.google.com/analytics/answer/10917952) gives utm_medium naming advice ('one unique utm_medium for each distinct channel'). It does not say UTM tags identify organic visits; GA4 does that from the referrer, which this form does not record. The title 'Leads saved with their landing URL' also no longer matches the body. -> "...then filter on utm_medium to separate paid leads from the rest." Or record the referrer as well and say leads referred by a search engine are organic. Bring the title and body back to the same point. | [truth | HUB_RULES 8] faq item 5: Escalated from the reviewer-c5-seo and reviewer-batch-m1 note. The page's own how-to makes launch the same as publishing: step 6 says 'before launch' and step 7 says 'Publish the page on your own domain'. URL Inspection only inspects a URL that Google can fetch on a verified property, so it cannot tell you before launch whether the page can be indexed. As written, this is untrue. -> Make URL Inspection the first check after publishing ("After publishing, run URL Inspection..."), and keep the Rich Results Test and canonical check before launch. | [craft | CONTENT_DEFECTS #21] howto_step_2_des; howto_step_4_des; howto_description: Three fields give one instruction, matching the top-ranking pages, with the words swapped. Make howto_description frame the method without restating step 2. | [craft | CONTENT_DEFECTS #21] feature_2; howto_step_4_des: This is the second instance of the same class: the form goes after the opening section, said in feature_2 and again in step 4. /ai-landing-page-builder/one-page-websit.note: [faq | HUB_RULES 5] faq: FAQ 4 asks 'How much does it cost to have a one-page website?' and the answer never states a cost: it lists what to budget for, with no figure and no 'it can cost nothing to build'. HUB_RULES 5 requires answers answer-first; the rubric requires each FAQ answered in its first sentence. Second instance of the class: FAQ 8 'Is it legal to use AI to create a website?' opens 'The US Copyright Office will not register material an AI generated without human authorship, though your own selection and arrangement of it can be protected.', which is about registration, not legality, and never says yes or no. -> FAQ 4: open with the answer in cost terms, e.g. 'Building one on Emergent's free tier costs nothing; the domain name is the cost you will always have, registered for a set term and renewed with your registrar.' (keep FAQ 3's credits point there, do not repeat it). FAQ 8: open with the direct answer the recorded Copyright Office source supports, e.g. 'Yes. The US Copyright Office registers works that contain AI-generated material, but only the parts a person authored, selected or arranged are protected.' then the advice sentence.
